title: So Rome's common view: natural as agreeable to nature and as present from origin, but not as opposed to supernatural
source_text: VI. Itaque Doctorum Ecclesiae Romanae communis sententia est, justitiam & sanctitatem, qua primus homo ante lapsum ornatus erat, naturalem quidem dici posse, quatenus naturale opponitur ei quod est contra naturam, & significat id quod est naturae consentaneum, & quod naturam non destruit, sed ornat & perficit: aut etiam quatenus naturale opponitur ei quod est adventitium, & significat id quod inest ab origine, seu a nativitate. Admittunt enim primum nostrum parentem in justitia fuisse creatum: & idcirco justitiam illam, qua in integritatis statu praeditus erat, vocant Originalem. Sed negant istam justitiam fuisse naturalem, quatenus naturale opponitur supernaturali; quia scilicet, ex eorum mente, ex principiis naturae non fluxit, sed fuit donum Dei gratuitum, quod hominem supra naturalem conditionem evexit.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the common opinion of the Doctors of the Roman Church is that the justice and sanctity with which the first man before the fall was adorned can indeed be called natural, insofar as natural is opposed to that which is against nature, and signifies what is agreeable to nature, and which does not destroy nature, but adorns and perfects it: or also insofar as natural is opposed to what is adventitious, and signifies what is present from origin, or from birth. For they admit that our first parent was created in justice: and therefore they call that justice, with which he was endowed in the state of integrity, Original. But they deny that this justice was natural, insofar as natural is opposed to supernatural; because namely, in their mind, it did not flow from the principles of nature, but was a gratuitous gift of God, which raised man above his natural condition.
pass_b_english: The common view of the Roman Church's teachers, then, is that the righteousness and holiness with which the first man was adorned before the fall can indeed be called natural in two senses. It is natural as opposed to what is against nature, meaning what suits nature and does not destroy it but adorns and perfects it. It is natural too as opposed to what is acquired, meaning what is there from the origin, or from birth.

For they grant that our first parent was created in righteousness, and so they call the righteousness he had in his unfallen state original righteousness. But they deny that it was natural as natural is opposed to supernatural, because in their view it did not flow from nature's principles but was God's free gift, which raised man above his natural condition.

choices.why: The gift lifts man above his natural level; 'raised' keeps the image without overstatement.
